newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea ruling party urges govt action to help Kia.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea ruling party urges govt action to help Kia.

text.p: South Korea's ruling New Korea Party on Wednesday urged the government to take action to solve the Kia Group's troubles.

"The government should not stand idly by any longer... It has to assume responsibility and make an aggressive effort to solve Kia problems," policy committee chairman Kim Zoong-wie said at a party meeting.
He also urged government ministries to cooperate.
The Kia Group was saved from imminent default last week when creditor banks designated the group for protection.
Since financial troubles in the nation's eighth largest conglomerate surfaced last week, South Koreans have worried about a chain of corporate failures.
Ssangyong Group, the nation's sixth-largest conglomerate, has also been hit by rumours of cash flow difficulties. The group has strongly denied the speculation.

Kim also said domestic financial institutions still appeared reluctant to grant loans to Kia's subcontractors, even though the monetary authorities have urged finance companies to keep their credit lines open to the subcontractors.
"As we witnessed in the Hanbo case, the government seemed unwilling to take responsibility and solve the problem," Kim said.
Hanbo Steel collapsed in January after piling up $5.8 billion in debts and is stilling looking for a buyer. The South Korean economy has since been rocked by a series of corporate financial troubles.
Kim said the government should try to prevent the credibility of Korean companies and financial institutions from suffering in world markets.
"Due to some groundless rumours, several corporates are suffering from liquidity problems. So the government should come up with measures to resolve the situation," he said.
